invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 sends a trader who opens a page from its task on the overview back to the overview on 'Save and continue', rather than on through the rest of the page's flow section. The service tells such a page by its own journey state, not by a marker in the page address: any save made outside the opening run and outside a change from the review page returns to the overview. increments.title: 'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader leave most pages for the overview without finishing them, so they can come back later. The backend already stores missing or empty answers. An answer that breaks its own format rule is still refused, because the service cannot store a value that does not fit its field, and consignment details, the CPH number page and the contact address page keep checking their answers before saving.
acceptanceCriteria: On origin of the import, 'What are you importing?', 'Main reason for import', 'Identification details', 'Additional details', 'Arrival details', 'Transit countries', the transporter page, 'Upload documents' and 'Roles and addresses', pressing 'Save and return to overview' with a required answer missing shows no error, saves what was entered and goes to the overview. increments.title: Port lists ordered airports, then seaports, then rail, from MDM's port type, with the port of exit reading and ordering like the port of entry, in animals and plants
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 puts airports before seaports, and Sam's 9 October ruling builds the order now: MDM's traffic field already gives every port its type, so nothing waits on MDM. Reference data maps the type through and orders the list airports, then seaports, then rail ports in a group of their own, each group A to Z by name ignoring letter case. Today reference data sorts by name alone, case-sensitively, so airports and seaports are mixed and names in capitals sort first. The plants frontend's place of landing list follows the same order in the same increment. List content stays what MDM serves: it is never edited in code. Design Release 2.1 labels each port of exit '<port name> - <port code>', as the port of entry options are labelled, and the 9 October ruling orders the port of exit lists as the port of entry list: airports, then seaports, then rail ports, each A to Z by name. Both lists read the same ports reference data serves, so the order and the label are built once for entry and exit.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference data's GET /ports-of-entry returns each port's type (airport, seaport or rail), taken from MDM's traffic field, alongside its code and name (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-172, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-176; repo:referencedata repo-referencedata-p1-031, repo-referencedata-p1-032, repo-referencedata-p1-033)

Locally, in CDP dev and in CDP test, the port of entry search on arrival details lists every airport first, then every seaport, then every rail port (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-173, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-174; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-019)

Within each group, ports are listed A to Z by name ignoring letter case, so a name written in capitals sorts among the other names that start with the same letter rather than ahead of them (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-175; repo:referencedata repo-referencedata-p1-030; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p4-076)
Non-breaking and doubled spaces in a port name are compared as single spaces, so such a name sorts where the same name with single spaces would (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-175)
The ordered list still holds every port reference data returns, and choosing a port still saves its code (repo:referencedata repo-referencedata-p1-031; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-027)

In the plants frontend, the place of landing search lists the ports in the same order: airports, then seaports, then rail ports, each group A to Z by name ignoring letter case (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-018; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p9-108, repo-plantsfrontend-p5-086)

Each 'Port of exit' option, on both the transit and the temporary admission selects, reads '<port name> - <port code>', the same label the port of entry options take, and choosing one still saves the port code (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-084; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-035; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p7-037; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p7-045; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p4-108)

Locally, in CDP dev and in CDP test, both 'Port of exit' selects list every airport first, then every seaport, then every rail port (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-165, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-172, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-173, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-174; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p7-046)

increments.title: The germinal commodity page offers today's 12 germinal lines, and the live-animals page no longer does
increments.detail: The 9 October afternoon ruling splits the germinal commodity work so the germinal set is not held up by the MDM catalogue. The germinal set's copy of today's 'What are you importing?' page carries the germinal search hint and offers the 12 germinal lines today's live-animals catalogue holds, named and coded as today, found through today's server-side search behind its Search button. Splitting today's lines between the sets is set architecture, not list content, so it goes ahead now: the live-animals catalogue gives up those 12 lines, and neither set offers the other's commodities. increments.title: Germinal Commodity details asks total gross weight, number of packages and temperature, and the backend stores and publishes them with interim typeCodes
increments.detail: The germinal set's copy of Commodity details asks, for each chosen species, an optional 'Total gross weight' in kilograms and a 'Number of packages', and always asks one optional 'Temperature' for the consignment. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row. The animals backend stores the gross weight as a decimal and the temperature on every line, and shows them back; neither is published, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no field for them. Until the germinal catalogue separates embryos from ova, each germinal trade line on GBN-AG carries an interim typeCode: SEMEN for a semen line and EMBRYO for a combined 'Embryos/Ova' line. The germinal set always asks the consignment's temperature; the animals backend stores it on the record and shows it back, but never publishes it, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no field for it. A germinal products notification is published on the same GBN-AG events and payload as a live-animals one, carrying only what that profile already carries and leaving out the sections the germinal set never asks, as the mapper already leaves out an unanswered section. No PIMS profile, trade-imports-schemas shape or trade-imports-dynamics-gateway mapping changes. Once germinal lines carry their own typeCode, every live-animal trade line carries typeCode LIVE_ANIMAL too.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before 'Number of packages'; left blank it shows no error. increments.title: Arrival details requires a means of transport, and arrival and transit return to where the trader came from

'Save and return to overview' lets a trader leave a part-finished page without a means of transport. The real service keeps every field check it has today (c-045): a page with any error saves nothing and shows the entries back, and an answer that cannot be stored, such as an impossible date, is refused even on 'Save and return to overview' (c-211).

increments.title: Identification counts as complete only when every animal is entered, and submit needs one entry per species when several are selected
increments.detail: Today the hub's Identification details row shows Complete straight after Commodity details, before any animal is identified, and stays Complete at 1 of 2. DR2.1 counts identification complete only when every animal of every selected species with identifier fields has a complete entry. For submitting, DR2.1 makes identification optional for a single species but needs at least one complete entry per species when more than one species is selected; the identification page itself shows no message for that rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Straight after Commodity details, with no animals entered, the hub's Identification details row does not show Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-002; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1)

A selected species with identifier fields but no number of animals keeps the row from showing Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068)
With one species selected and no identification entered, the notification can be submitted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)

With two species with identifier fields selected and one of them without any complete entry, submitting is refused; once each has at least one complete entry, submitting goes ahead. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-020)

The real service does not offer these commodities: today's live-animal catalogue holds five commodities, none of them these. The 9 October afternoon ruling puts commodity catalogue work behind the MDM commodity integration, so this row waits until pigs, sheep and goats reach the catalogue from MDM; each selected pig, sheep or goat species then gets a panel asking for one ear tag per animal.

increments.title: Germinal identification asks once per species for donor, dates and identification number, and the backend stores them unpublished
increments.detail: Germinal products are identified once per species, whatever their number of packages. The germinal set's copy of Identification details shows each germinal species one editable form with V4's four optional fields, saved by the page's own buttons and prefilled with what was saved. The animals backend stores the four fields and shows them back; none is published, because gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 has no field for them. The germinal products set's own copy of Identification details counts packages, not animals: its Selected commodities quantity column reads 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved number of packages, where the live-animals page shows Number of animals. This is the one germinal requirement on this page's summary that the animal-identification area holds; the germinal-products area holds the rest of the germinal identification page. The germinal set collects a donor name or ID, a collection date, a production date and an identification mark for each germinal species. The PIMS profile has no field for them, so the animals backend is their only home: it stores them, the service shows them back, and the GBN-AG payload carries none of them. Where they sit on the record (on the per-item identifier entries of each line, as animal identifiers do, or on the species line) is decided in the build from the real model.

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats and dogs, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for each pet's permanent address on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. Cats, dogs and ferrets need one; other live mammals, which share their commodity code 01061900, do not. It is built now for cats and dogs over today's catalogue, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the catalogue holds them. The page has a card for each animal that needs one, showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment with cats or dogs has a 'Permanent address' section on the consignment addresses page explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats alone there is no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-085, p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-081; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-018)

A consignment of cattle, horses or fish has no permanent address section, and opening the permanent address page for it sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-109; document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-012, p6-015)

The permanent address page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the heading 'Permanent address', the browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and a back link to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021, p9-032, p9-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-109, p13-110; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-082, p3-108)
The animal identification page no longer asks for any address field (document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-058; trace:e2e p6-028)

The page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as were entered for each species, headed with the scientific name and a running number such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no card (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-037, p9-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-091, p13-111; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-084)

Each card shows the animal's entered identifiers in inset text as 'label: value', such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1', leaving out blank ones, and shows no inset when none are entered (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-111)

Each card asks 'Select an address' with the options 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', neither chosen when the page first opens; once a place of destination is given, the first option's hint is that address on one line, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-040, p9-041, p9-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-092, p7-094, p7-095, p13-112; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-085)

'Enter a new address' has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.', and choosing it reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, with 'Email address' before 'Phone number' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-042, p9-043, p9-050, p9-051; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-093, p7-097, p7-098, p13-113; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-086, p3-090)

The page ends with the 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page (document:dr1-parity-notes p1-055, p1-056, p1-058; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-104; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-077)

An animal saved as 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' has the place of destination's name, address, country, email and phone as its permanent address on the review page, and reopening the permanent address page shows that option selected (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-067, p9-068; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-115; prototype:dr2-1-specs p4-039)

A new address saved with a county and no address line 2 reopens with 'Enter a new address' selected, each value in its own field: the county in 'County', the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code', with country United Kingdom (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-068; trace:e2e p6-032)

An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and returns to the consignment addresses page, and the permanent address section stays incomplete, holding the notification back from submission, until every animal that needs one has an address with a name (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-062, p9-063, p9-074; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-102; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-089)

increments.title: The permanent address page checks each new address, names the animal in every error, and answers errors as an error page
increments.detail: With several animals on one page, the trader must be told which animal each error is about. A new address's name, first line, town, postcode, email and phone are required exactly when 'Enter a new address' is chosen, and the same-as-destination choice cannot be used before a place of destination exists. increments.title: The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what type of address is being added and what it can be used for, and Sam's 9 October ruling keeps both answers because a question the service asks must persist and DR1 asked for address pickers filtered by role (c-176). Today the address-book record is untyped and its API carries no type or use, so nothing can keep those answers, and the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 role-filtered pickers have nothing to filter on. Afterwards an API caller can create, read and update an address with its type and uses, in a field shape the address-book service designs in its own conventions, and addresses saved before the change still read back.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an address through the address book API with its address type and one or more uses (place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address) stores them, and reading the address back by id returns the same type and the same uses (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-115, p1-116)
Updating an address through the API with a different set of uses replaces its uses with the new set, and the read-back shows the new set (repo:addressbook p2-071; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079)

A create or update carrying a use outside those six is refused with a 400 validation problem whose errors name the uses, and nothing is saved (repo:addressbook p1-039, p1-045; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
An address created without a type or uses, and every address saved before this change, is still accepted and reads back with no type and no uses (repo:addressbook p1-001, p1-003)

The address book's locked API contract describes the type and uses on the create and update requests and on the read response, with the six allowed uses (repo:addressbook p2-097, p2-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-064, p7-065)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings. Pass 1 slice on its own: the typed record is the foundation the add form's uses question, the list's type tabs (address-book-list area) and DR1 inc-047/inc-048 rest on, so it lands first and gates. Observable through the API in every environment the tests repo's address book API client reaches (local stack and CDP). The field names and shape are the address-book service's (c-176; ruling 9 October claims 66, 70, 116), so no criterion names the prototype's 'primary type' or 'address book type'. c-176 leaves the rejection of stray 'type' and 'role' fields for the service to keep or replace. Type and uses stay optional on the API so a journey's handshake add and every existing record keep saving; the add form makes a use required outside a journey. Updates fully replace the editable fields, so the edit page must post the stored type and uses back; that is the edit row's criterion. Decision kept: refuse an unknown use with a 400 (validation clause of ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
increments.gate: Check the type and uses field names, the six use values and how a record without them reads back in the locked contract, before the add form, the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 address pickers build on it.

increments.title: Adding an address starts by choosing its type
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added before any fields, because the type decides the form and the uses offered next. Today the address book's add is the address form itself. Afterwards 'Add a new address' on the address book opens a new 'Choose an address type' page, on a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape, offering three types: 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch'. 'Transporter' is left out until transporter management is decided (ruling 9 October pm, c-306). Choosing a type moves on to the address form, which stays where it is today (the page the animals frontend's handshake links to), retitled 'Add address and contact details' and able to go back to the type page. The chosen type is remembered while the add is in progress and cleared when it starts afresh or saves. The type choices Design Release 2.1 offers when adding an address, in order and with their hints, which also name the categories the list's tabs and Type filter group by. The choice itself is made on the add-and-edit area's type step, so this requirement belongs in that step's row.
acceptanceCriteria: From the address book list, 'Add a new address' opens a page with the caption 'Add a new address', the heading 'Choose an address type', a radio group whose legend repeats the heading visually hidden, and a 'Back' link to the address book list (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-001, p16-003, p16-004, p16-005, p16-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-039; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-105, p6-106, p6-112)

The options are, in order: 'Origin or Consignor' (hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'), 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' (hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer') and 'Branch' (hint 'Branch address'), with no 'Transporter' option, and a 'Continue' button (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-006 to p16-010, p16-012; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-040 to p16-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-107 to p6-111, p6-113; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-046; c-306)

Continuing with no type chosen shows 'Select an address type' inline on the radios and in a 'There is a problem' summary whose link goes to the first option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-016; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-045; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-114, p6-115)

Choosing 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' or 'Branch' and continuing opens the address form, which posts back to itself and shows the caption 'Add new address', the heading 'Add address and contact details', no notification status banner, and a 'Back' link to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-018, p16-019, p16-021, p16-022, p16-023, p16-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-047, p16-053, p16-069; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-116, p6-117, p6-118; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-090)
Opening the address form outside a notification journey with no address type chosen goes to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-020)

Going back from the address form to 'Choose an address type' shows the chosen type selected; opening 'Add a new address' again from the address book starts with no type selected and empty fields, and after a save the next add starts empty (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-002, p16-011, p16-087)

The browser titles of 'Choose an address type', the address form and the edit page read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', such as 'Choose an address type - Import notification service - GOV.UK', keeping the 'Error: ' prefix when a page shows errors (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-053, p16-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-117, p6-158; trace:ins-fit p1-003, p3-003)

A notification journey's handshake into the address form still opens the form directly, without 'Choose an address type', and the save still hands the new address id back to the journey (repo:insfrontend p3-095 to p3-107; trace:e2e p15-006, p15-007; c-106)

The address types offered when adding an address read, in this order and with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'), 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'), then, after a divider, 'Branch Address' ('This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'); no 'Transporter' type is offered. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-105 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-111; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-095; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-046)

Rewritten for Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling (point 2, claims p2-031 to p2-046; c-306): 'Choose an address type' is built now with three options and no 'Transporter', so req-1198 (the Transporter option) moves out of this row to the blocked transporter hand-over row (inc-074). req-1199 now places 'Branch' third. 'Branch Address') differs from req-1196/1197/1199's three grouped options, so it is left to that area's drafter and the combiner to place, and is not restated here. req-2045 (three radios, no Transporter), which areas.json gives to no area, is this row's behaviour: the combiner adds it here.

increments.title: Address book list: Design Release 2.1 intro, filter disclosure, search control, table cells, empty state and a banner that stays
increments.detail: The INS address book list changes to Design Release 2.1's layout and copy. The intro is reworded and set in large body text, 'Add a new address' moves directly under it, and search moves into a collapsed 'Filter addresses' disclosure, a GOV.UK details component, with a plain 'Search' label, a placeholder instead of a hint and an icon-only search button that is a real submit button. The 'Clear search' link goes. The table shows a multi-word name on two lines and every stored address line on its own line. An empty book or a search with no match shows the same table with 'Showing 0 of 0' instead of a message, and the success banner stays until the user leaves or reloads the page, so its hiding script is removed. Every part works without JavaScript. All of this is the same list page and template, so it is one review.

(prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-005; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-083)

(prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-008; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-085, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-099; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-046, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-098)

increments.title: Saving a new address with its uses
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what an address can be used for on the add-details step and saves the ticked uses with it, then shows the user the new address among its kind. Afterwards an Origin or Consignor address offers 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor' after a section break, a use is required once the fields are valid, the save stores the address's type and ticked uses in the address book, and the user lands on the address book list showing that type, with the new address first, a reworded success banner, its full address and searchable by its uses. The k6 performance suite's address-book scenarios follow the new add.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Origin or Consignor' the address and contact fields show straight away with no address search, then a section break, then the uses question with the legend 'What can this address be used for?', the hint 'Select where this address can be used' and the checkboxes 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor', with no hint on either option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-048, p16-052, p16-053, p16-054, p16-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054, p16-065, p16-066; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-119, p6-120)

With the address and contact fields valid and no use ticked, saving shows 'Select what this address can be used for' inline and in the error summary, linked to the first use option; while any field is invalid the uses are not checked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-076; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-077, p16-129; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-135)

Saving stores the address in the address book with its type and every ticked use, and a use posted that does not belong to the chosen type is not stored (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-078, p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-056-m1, p16-081)

After saving an Origin or Consignor address the user lands on the address book list showing Origin or Consignor addresses, with the new address listed first and a 'View' link to its own page (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-083, p16-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-079, p16-081, p16-082; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137, p6-139; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-075, p1-091)
The list then shows a 'Success' banner reading '<name> address added to your address book' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-085; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-080)

The added address reads as address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode joined by commas, leaving out blanks, with the country shown separately (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-080, p15-084; trace:ins-fit p1-058)
The added address is found by the address book search on its name, on a use such as 'Consignor', on part of its address and on its country (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-082)

Run against the local stack, the k6 performance suite's address-book session add and its background-volume adds choose 'Origin or Consignor', tick 'Place of origin', post the INS front door's own address field names and pass their 'address added' and 'background address added' checks on the save's return to the list showing Origin or Consignor addresses; its edit scenario and background-volume gate pass unchanged (repo:perftests p2-027, p2-028, p2-030, p2-032, p2-035, p2-036, p2-047; c-225)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings, except that the list's category tabs it lands on are now three (the Transporter tab waits; ruling 9 October pm p2-045), which does not touch an Origin or Consignor save. Depends on the typed record, the type step and the add-details form rows. Cross-area: the landing view needs the address book list's type tabs, and the search on a use needs the list's search over uses (address-book-list area), so this row depends on the list rows that build them (inc-067, inc-069 today). The list's tab parameter, its values and the uses field name are the INS service's to name (ruling 9 October claims 66, 91), so no criterion names a query string. The INS frontend's address book client and its stub-mode stub must carry the type and uses. req-1260 is built without the prototype's nameless fallback: a save always has a name. In journey mode the add ticks the role's use and returns to the journey with no address book banner; that is req-1284's row, and a journey-mode save must keep working here. Pass 1 slices combined: the uses question, its validation, the save and the return all exercise one save and one review. The k6 suite (req-1870) is changed here, on this row's branch name, as c-225 settles: this is the row whose save first needs a type and a use and returns to the list filtered by type.

The details page lives where the real services hold transporter records, in their conventions. Blocked: the address book's transporter rows wait on transporter requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: Each row of the transporter list ends with a 'View details' link whose visually hidden text names the transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-026; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-089; conflicts:c-052)

Following a transporter's 'View details' opens that transporter's details page, showing its record, and its Back link returns to the same notification's transporter list. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-090, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p9-047; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-106; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 21)

sources.ref: claims 18, 21: details page in the real services' conventions

openQuestions: Blocked on transporter requirements: whether the service manages transporters at all, and whether the address book or some other functionality does it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 31-37, 43, c-285). The ruling names nobody to decide it; whoever owns transporter requirements decides, and the transporter area is then re-distilled.
notes: Blocked by ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 43 (c-285). Kept apart: it needs transporter records with a details page (the address-book rows it depends on) and the reshaped list (inc-037).

Theme moved to transporters: the address book's transporter rows wait on transporter management with the transporter pages they hand over to (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 35 and 36). Keeping them in address-book made that whole theme wait for the transporters theme through rows that cannot build yet.

increments.title: The INS add page reached from a journey shows Design Release 2.1's 'Add address and contact details' page
increments.detail: When a trader follows 'Add a new address' from a role picker, the INS front door's add page (reached through today's handshake, which stays: c-106) shows Design Release 2.1's page instead of today's 'Add address details' form. It is headed 'Add address and contact details' under the caption 'Add new address', keeps the trader oriented with the notification's status block, groups its fields under 'Address' and 'Contact details', relabels the name field, drops County, and gives every personal-data field its autocomplete hint (GOV.UK pattern and WCAG 1.3.5, c-109). Observable in the INS frontend's own fit suite (with the handshake query), on the compose stack and in CDP; in the animals frontend's stub mode there is no INS frontend and the pickers show no add link (c-106), so that environment is not named.
acceptanceCriteria: Following 'Add a new address' from any role picker opens a page headed 'Add address and contact details' whose browser title is 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-002, p7-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-058-m1; trace:e2e p9-055)
The page shows the caption 'Add new address' above its heading (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-059)
The page shows the notification's status block: a 'Draft' tag and the notification's reference, as the journey's own pages do (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-004; trace:e2e p9-055-m1, p8-090)
The first section heading reads 'Address' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-005; prototype:dr2-1-source p8-083)
The second section heading reads 'Contact details' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-005; prototype:dr2-1-source p8-085)
The name field is labelled 'Name or organisation' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-083; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-006; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-060)
The page has no County field (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-083; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-060; trace:e2e p9-062)

The fields carry the browser autocomplete hints organization (name), address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 (town or city), postal-code, email and tel (repo:frontend p9-103-m1; trace:e2e p9-065; conflicts:c-109)
notes: Unchanged from the last distil: none of its requirements changed. Combines the page-frame slice (heading, title, caption, status block) with the field-copy slice (section headings, name label, no county, autocomplete): both change the same INS add-details template in journey mode, so building them apart would repeat the same set-up and ladder. The page is the INS add-details step the address-book-add-and-edit area restructures: combiner, keep it depending on that area's add-details rows (inc-061, inc-062); only the status block is journey-specific. The address book record keeps its optional county, left empty (req-642 deltaNote).

increments.title: The journey add page splits origin-side and destination-side roles, with Design Release 2.1's country placeholder and messages
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets place of origin and consignor addresses be anywhere, entered by hand with every field shown at once, while consignee, importer and place of destination addresses are UK addresses. Today the INS add page is the same for every role, with the full country list. This row makes the page reached from a role picker follow that split, gives the origin-side Country select the 'Select one' placeholder, and changes the required-field messages to Design Release 2.1's wording. Today's length and email-format checks stay alongside (c-108). Until the address lookup is a real feature the destination-side pages open on manual entry, with every field shown and no search (c-106, c-217, req-1830). Observable in the INS frontend's fit suite with the handshake query, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: Reached from the place of origin or consignor picker, the page shows every address and contact field at once and lets the trader choose any country the Country select offers (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-081, p8-090; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-027; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-077)

Reached from the consignee, importer or place of destination picker, the page still opens with every address and contact field shown and no address search (conflicts:c-106; conflicts:c-217; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-182)

Reached from the consignee, importer or place of destination picker, the Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', preselected, and the saved address's country is United Kingdom whatever is posted (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-082; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-044; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-072, p3-078, p3-079, p3-080)
On the place of origin and consignor pages the Country select's first option reads 'Select one' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-084; trace:e2e p9-064; conflicts:c-107)

Saving with a blank name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', in the error summary and against the name field, the summary link reaching it (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-100; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-030; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-066)
Saving with a blank postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-103; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-033)
Saving from an origin-side page with no country chosen shows 'Select a country' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-104; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-034)
Phone number is required: saving with it blank shows 'Enter a phone number' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-106; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-036)

An over-long postcode or a badly formed email address is still refused with today's messages ('Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer', 'Enter an email address in the correct format') (repo:frontend p9-115, p9-120; conflicts:c-108)
notes: Combines the role-split slice with the country placeholder and the four required-field message changes: the same page, the same validation set-up and the same per-role fixtures. The destination-side manual-entry criterion is req-1830, adopted as exists (no search exists today); it stays as a 'still' criterion because this row reshapes exactly those pages, but req-1830 is not listed in requirements. The country list's content is its own row (req-644). The address-book-add-and-edit area changes the same messages and the same type split in the address book API: combiner, keep the dependency on inc-060 rather than building the messages twice. Today's length and email-format checks are kept by ruling (c-108; req-668, req-669 exist).

increments.title: A new address added from the journey can also be saved for the other roles on its side
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets one new address be saved for more roles than the one it was added from. The add page reached from a role picker asks 'What else should this address be used for?', offering only the other roles on the same side, and the saved address book record carries the role it was added for plus every use ticked. Today the record has no field for roles; the address book's uses field is built in inc-059. Observable in the INS frontend's fit suite with the handshake query (the stubbed address book receives the uses), on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: The page asks 'What else should this address be used for?' as a group of checkboxes (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-092; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-015; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-062)

The question's hint reads 'This address is being added as a <Role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', naming Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer or Place of destination, with 'an' before Importer (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-092, p8-093; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-016; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-062, p3-077 to p3-079)

The checkboxes offer only the other roles on the same side, each labelled with the role name alone: place of origin offers 'Consignor'; consignor offers 'Place of origin'; consignee offers 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'; importer offers 'Consignee' and 'Place of destination'; place of destination offers 'Consignee' and 'Importer' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-094 to p8-096; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-017 to p7-022; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-063, p3-075)
No checkbox is preselected and saving with none ticked raises no error (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-097, p8-098)
A posted use not offered for the role is discarded, and the ticked uses stay ticked when the page is shown again with errors (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-108; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-038)

Saving an address added from the consignee picker with 'Importer' ticked stores a record whose uses, as the address book's read-one API returns them to the services that read it, are consignee and importer (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-110, p8-114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-061; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-113; trace:e2e p8-012)
notes: Unchanged from the last distil. Combines the uses question (legend, hint, options, no preselection, discard) with saving the uses: the question has no observable effect until the save carries it. The address book record's uses field and its API contract are the address-book-add-and-edit area's, built in inc-059, so this row depends on it (and on inc-077) rather than adding addressbook to its repos. The address book's own add uses a different legend and hint; the journey page keeps Design Release 2.1's journey wording.

increments.title: A notification journey's add opens Design Release 2.1's add page in journey mode, and saving or cancelling lands where Design Release 2.1 says
increments.detail: A trader adding an address from a notification's party picker keeps today's handshake to the INS address book, sees Design Release 2.1's add page in journey mode, and on saving or cancelling lands back on the journey page Design Release 2.1 names, with its success banner. Observable on the compose stack and in CDP, where both frontends run; in the animals frontend's stub mode the pickers show no add link (c-106). A trader adding an address from a notification's party picker keeps today's handshake to the INS address book (c-106), because which service serves the add page and writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. Reached that way, the INS add page shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page in journey mode: it skips 'Choose an address type', opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies with the role's use ticked, and returns through the journey's address-return to the page each button names.
acceptanceCriteria: The add page has a 'Back' link that returns to the picker of the role the address is being added for (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-080; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-025; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-065)
The primary button reads 'Save and select' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-064)

'Save and select' saves the address to the address book, puts a copy on the notification for the role, and lands on the Consignment addresses page, where that role shows the address with a 'Change' link (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-110; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-054, p7-055, p7-059; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-076)

A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the address to the address book without selecting it and lands on the role's picker, where the new address is listed first and no address is selected for the role (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-039, p7-041, p7-060; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-068)

After either save the landing page shows a success banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-040, p7-055)

The page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link that lands on the notification's hub and saves nothing to the address book or the notification (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-024, p7-064)

The end-to-end suite drives 'Save and select', 'Save and return to address page' and 'Cancel and return to hub' from each of the five role pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination), on the compose stack and in CDP (repo:tests p5-032, p5-033; trace:e2e p9-077)
The journey's address-return still refuses an unknown fulfilment or a stale handshake token, for each of the new landings (repo:frontend p9-139, p9-141; conflicts:c-106)

On the compose stack and in CDP, 'Add a new address' on a notification's party page still hands over to the INS address book's add page through today's handshake, only for a registered journey, with the return built on the server (repo:insfrontend p3-095 to p3-107; trace:e2e p15-006, p15-007; c-106)

Reached by the handshake, the INS add page does not ask 'Choose an address type' and opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies, with that role's use ticked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-088, p16-091; c-106)

'Save and select' saves the address and commits its copy to the notification for the role, landing on the Consignment addresses page; 'Save and return to address page' saves it and lands on the role's picker with nothing selected; 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing; each lands through the journey's address-return (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-088 to p16-095; repo:tests p5-034 to p5-036; c-106)

Landing back in the journey shows the journey page's own banner and not the INS address book's banner, and the journey still refuses a return with an unknown fulfilment or a stale handshake token (repo:insfrontend p3-108 to p3-112, p3-138; trace:e2e p15-008, p15-009)

When the INS add page is reached from a notification journey, it skips 'Choose an address type' and opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies, with that role already counted as the address's use (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-007; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-092; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p9-055; c-106)
notes: Combines the drafts of the party-address-add-and-edit, address-book-add-and-edit areas for this row: they change the same page, record or set-up, so building them apart would repeat it.

Combines the buttons-and-copy slice (Save and select, Save and return to address page, Cancel and return to hub, Back) with the landing and banner slice and the every-picker proof: all three change the one return contract between the INS add page and the journey's address-return, and the proof is of the same round trip. repos is in merge order: frontend before insfrontend, because the journey's address-return must accept each new landing before the INS page sends it. Combiner: the existing row also covers req-1284 (journey mode of the INS add page, skipping 'Choose an address type'), which belongs to the address-book-add-and-edit area; this draft lists only this area's requirements and leaves out req-1284's three criteria (journey-mode type skip, the INS banner not shown on landing, the registered live-animals handshake). Merge the two drafts back into inc-080 as before, keeping its id and gate. Depends on inc-077.

Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings. Combiner: merge into inc-080 with the party-address area's draft (req-637, req-671 to req-675, req-678), as the backlog already does: both change the one return contract between the INS add page and the journey's address-return. req-1958 (journey mode skips the type step), which areas.json gives to no area, is this row's behaviour and belongs here. Observable on the compose stack and in CDP, where both frontends run; in the animals frontend's stub mode the pickers show no add link (c-106), so the fit suites do not observe the hand-over. repos lists frontend before insfrontend because the journey's address-return must accept each landing before the INS page sends it. Depends on the type-step and add-details rows through inc-077. A germinal products notification uses the same handshake with its own INS return entry (ruling 9 October claim 61), built by the germinal area's rows, not here.
req-1958 (journey mode skips 'Choose an address type' and counts the role as the address's use) is added here by the combiner, as the address-book-add-and-edit draft asks.
increments.gate: Look at the changed handshake return before anything builds on it: each of the three actions and the Back link lands on the right journey page from all five pickers, and the address-return still refuses an unknown fulfilment or a stale token.

increments.title: Destination-side journey add pages find UK addresses by a search that works without JavaScript
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's consignee, importer and place of destination add pages, reached from the journey through the INS frontend's address book (c-106), start with a UK address search, as the address book's own 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' step does. The 9 October afternoon ruling (c-287) has the version that works without JavaScript built: a search form submitted to the server by its Search button, results on the returned page, and a pick that fills the fields from the INS backend's address lookup (c-178). Sam's 9 October ruling blocks all of it in every environment until the address lookup becomes a real feature; until then the pages open on manual entry (inc-078), and the area is re-distilled once the lookup lands (c-217).
acceptanceCriteria: The consignee, importer and place of destination add pages and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step start with a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search button whose accessible name is 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042, p7-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-069)
With JavaScript turned off, pressing 'Search' submits the search to the server and the returned page lists the matching UK addresses (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-046, p1-047; conflicts:c-287)

Submitting the search lists matching UK addresses from the address lookup under 'Address search results', each a choice showing the organisation name where the lookup has one and the lookup's full one-line address, and no Northern Ireland address (postcode starting 'BT') is offered (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-087; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-053, p7-063; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-073; conflicts:c-178)

Picking a result fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all editable, leaving the name for the trader where the lookup gives none and leaving email address and phone number empty; earlier error messages stay until the next submit (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-089; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048 to p7-050, p7-048-m1, p7-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-074; conflicts:c-178)
Picking a result whose lookup address has a locality keeps the locality in the filled form, in address line 2 with the street (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048-m2; conflicts:c-178)
openQuestions: Blocked (req-647, req-648, req-650, req-651 blockedBy; c-217): the INS backend's address lookup must become a real feature. Today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Who: the team building the INS address lookup. Once it lands this area is re-distilled, which settles which environments the search runs in and what else it needs (ruling 2026-10-09 p1-178, p1-180).
notes: Rewritten for the 9 October afternoon ruling (c-287): the search is a server-submitted form that works without JavaScript, so 'typing lists results' became 'submitting the search lists results', and the bold match text is gone (it is req-1957, filtering as the trader types, not this area's). The JavaScript-only and design-dependent parts that were in this row (the live-region result count req-649, 'Enter address manually' req-652, the search-only layout req-653 and its errors req-654) move to their own waiting-on-design row, so this row no longer waits on design question 10. Still blocked on the lookup. Built on the address book's own search row (inc-072, also blocked) and the manual-entry page of inc-078.

increments.title: The journey add page's Country select offers the countries reference-data serves from MDM
increments.detail: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the trader picks the address's country by hand. Sam's 9 October ruling takes the MDM block off this row (c-107): the select offers reference-data's unfiltered country list, which is what MDM serves, and no list is typed or edited in code. Where MDM's content differs from Design Release 2.1's 42 entries, such as the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies, that is MDM's content to change. The stub tidy-up regenerates the local country fixture from MDM, so the names and counts the page's checks expect move to the recaptured fixture. The select stays a plain select, not the accessible autocomplete. Observable in the INS frontend's fit suite, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the Country select offers every country in reference-data's unfiltered /countries response for that environment, with the names it serves, and no country it does not serve (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-129, p1-132, p1-143; conflicts:c-107)

On the compose stack the select holds as many countries, with the same names, as the stub's regenerated MDM country fixture serves unfiltered, not today's 32 sovereign states (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-150, p1-155, p1-162; trace:e2e p9-064)

The end-to-end and fit checks of the select take their country names and counts from the captured reference-data fixture, and no country list is typed by hand in them (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-144, p1-159, p1-160)
notes: Unchanged from the last distil. Depends on inc-078 (the origin-side page) and on the stub tidy-up row at the head of the reference-lists theme (inc-173), because ruling p1-149 has that row change the names and counts these checks assert. The stub tidy-up owns regenerating the stub and capture fixtures; this row only aligns the add page and its checks. Today the INS select pins United Kingdom first and drops GB from the list; that ordering is not list content and is kept.

increments.title: Welsh for the redesigned address book list, view and delete pages
increments.detail: Every new or changed English string on the address book list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off, so a Welsh user sees the same Design Release 2.1 page rather than today's. The Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab.
acceptanceCriteria: With Welsh selected, the list, view and delete pages show a Welsh string for every piece of copy the Design Release 2.1 rows added or changed (intro, 'Filter addresses', 'Search', the placeholder, the three tab names and headings, column headers, Type labels and options, 'County (optional)', 'Delete this address?', 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', 'This action cannot be undone.', 'Yes, delete', 'No, cancel', the banners and the page titles), and no English string is left. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-047)

Today's Welsh strings for the replaced copy, such as 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau' and 'Dileu cyfeiriad', no longer show. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to repo-insfrontend-p2-105)
Each new Welsh string is visibly marked, where the Welsh copy is kept, as an unreviewed machine draft awaiting Welsh Language Standards sign-off. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098)

sources.ref: claim 36, third bullet (inc-083 no longer depends on inc-075; Transporter Welsh waits)

notes: A requirement sits in one row, and req-1186 spans the copy every other buildable row in this area changes, so it is the last of them and checks the whole set. Builders of the earlier rows add a Welsh machine draft beside each English string they add, so the Welsh page never falls back to English for long; this row completes and verifies it. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling (claim 36) takes the dependency on the blocked Transporter-tab row away: the Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab. Depends on every buildable row in this area: the list row, the return-path row (and through it the view and delete rows) and the search row (and through it the tabs and Type-filter rows).

increments.title: Welsh drafts for the new add and edit copy
increments.detail: The address book keeps English and Welsh copy side by side. Changing only the English would leave the Welsh describing the old pages. Afterwards every new or changed English string on the add and edit pages built now has a Welsh entry, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book's Welsh copy has an entry for every new or changed English string on 'Choose an address type', the add-details step (every type's layout, the uses question and every error message) and the edit page, and no add or edit page shows an English string where the Welsh copy is in use (repo:insfrontend p3-113 to p3-120)
The Welsh copy stays marked as an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:insfrontend p3-113)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings. Depends on every todo row in this area that adds or changes English copy (validation messages, type step, add-details form, uses and save, manual entry for Destination and Branch, edit). It does not wait for the blocked rows (the address search rows and the Transporter hand-over); each drafts its own Welsh when it is built. Kept as one sweep so the Welsh is checked once against the finished English. The combiner may fold it into the address book list area's Welsh row, which edits the same copy file.

increments.title: Roles and addresses page: intro, warning, Consignor name, named add links and full addresses
increments.detail: Brings the live-animals roles and addresses page's words and rows in line with Design Release 2.1 inside the summary list DR1 kept (c-087). The page gains an intro paragraph, the fraud warning loses its full stop, the consignor party is called 'Consignor' rather than 'Consignor or exporter', every empty row offers a link that names what it adds instead of a bare 'Add', and an answered row shows the whole chosen address, not just the name, so a trader can check every address without opening each picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm carries the 'Consignor' rename to the high-risk plants frontend's consignor picker and its check-answers label in the same change, so the two services name the party the same way. Every new or changed string carries a Welsh machine draft.
acceptanceCriteria: Under the heading 'Consignment addresses' the page shows the paragraph 'Add all the addresses that are involved in the consignment.' increments.title: Role-filtered party pickers on one page
increments.detail: Gives every address-book record one or more roles and makes each live-animals party picker, and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, offer only the organisation's addresses for its role, all on one page. The address book stores the roles and lists one role's addresses unpaginated; each frontend asks for its picker's role. Records saved before roles existed are offered on every picker until given a role, so nobody loses an address on a guess. Stub mode in both frontends gets roles on its canned records so it filters too. Because each page is now one role's addresses, pagination and the 'Selected address' inset go. Search stays the server search behind the submitting search button; filtering as the trader types waits on design in its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: On the compose stack, an address saved with only the consignee role appears on the consignee picker and not on the place of origin, consignor, importer or place of destination pickers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-070, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-047)

An address saved with the exporter role appears on the consignor picker; there is no separate exporter picker (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-064, prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)
An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-065)

On the compose stack, the high-risk plants consignor picker offers only addresses carrying the consignor role and the plants place of destination picker only those carrying the place of destination role, each with the role-less records too (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-027; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-019)

An address-book record with no role appears on all five animals pickers and on both plants pickers, on the compose stack and in CDP (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-027)

The address book returns an organisation's addresses for one requested role in a single unpaginated list, carrying each record's roles, and never returns a deleted record (document:dr1-parity-notes document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-022, document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-023; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-052; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-115)

Each animals picker and each plants picker lists every address it offers on one page, with no page-number links and no Previous or Next links, however many addresses the role has (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-052, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-056, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-027; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-012)

No animals or plants picker shows a 'Selected address:' inset; a party's chosen address shows as its checked row when the picker is reopened (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-050, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-055; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-041)

Submitting a search still narrows the one-page list on the server in both frontends (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-073)
notes: Rewritten on this re-distil. req-592 (filtering as the trader types) leaves this row: ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm blocks it on design question 5, so it sits in its own blocked row and this row builds now (c-094). Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm also extends req-594, req-595, req-608, req-611, req-612 and req-613 to the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers and its stub book (c-101), so plantsfrontend joins the row. Combines role filtering (address book roles and role-scoped list, each frontend asking by role, untyped fallback, stub roles) with one-page listing and dropping the 'Selected address' inset, because c-094 rules they land together: one page is only sensible once it is one role's addresses, and the inset only existed to carry a selection across pages. c-100: DR1's typed-record block is lifted; the typed record is built in trade-imports-address-book. Its field shape for roles is the address book's own design (req-611); the record's type and uses are inc-059's, in the address-book theme, which this row depends on, and the role-scoped list sits in the same address-book code, so the combiner should check the theme boundary there. c-101: untyped records show on every picker until given a role, in the compose stack and CDP alike, never filtered on a guess. Both frontends' address-book services stay read-only (c-106, req-618). Giving a record its roles through the INS address book's add and edit pages belongs to the address-book-add-and-edit and party-address-add-and-edit areas; on the compose stack the role-carrying records these criteria use are set-up for a one-page assertion through the address book, which the test rules allow. The picker's search must still answer a 255-character term (req-1828, exists, driven by the k6 scripts). The tests repo's pagination and later-page-selection tests (repo-tests-p5-013, p5-018, p5-020) and the plants picker specs change with it. Theme: consignment-parties.

The same-as row, the place of origin country search, the live filter row and the germinal set's copy of the pickers build on this.

The button copies the source party's record onto the notification as an independent copy, so a later change to the source does not ripple through.

increments.title: Place of origin picker searches by country
increments.detail: Gives the live-animals place of origin picker the country search Design Release 2.1 draws, built as ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm directs: its own label, hint and placeholder, and the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of the countries MDM serves through reference-data, with a button that submits the chosen country so the server keeps only the addresses in that country. Without JavaScript the native select and the button do the same. Filtering as the trader types waits on design and is not part of this row.

The other four pickers keep their 'Search' label and free-text search, and every new string has a Welsh machine-draft counterpart (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p9-053, repo-frontend-p9-089)

notes: Rewritten on this re-distil: ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm (c-102) makes req-624 the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select of MDM's countries with a submitting button, narrowed on the server; the prototype's own country widget, its as-you-type row filtering and its custom announcements are set aside (their claims are overruled), and the as-you-type country filter waits on design as req-1951, in another area. The placeholder is built now, which only the autocomplete can show. Combines the place of origin picker's label, hint, placeholder and country search: one picker, one search control. The search keeps the real service's field name and action (req-1829 out of scope, req-1828 exists); the native select may need a country value alongside the free-text q the k6 scripts drive, which the plan stage settles without breaking req-1828. The country list comes from the frontend's existing countries service (reference-lists theme); the accessible autocomplete component is the journey foundation's, used here, not changed. increments.title: The CPH number page follows Design Release 2.1: who is asked, its help and hint, a blank save, and where it goes
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for a county parish holding (CPH) number for every live animal kept on a holding. In the live-animals set every commodity but horses (0101) and the pet code 01061900 (cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals) gets the question, built now over the five commodities today's catalogue holds, so the same rule takes in pigs, sheep, poultry and the rest once the MDM catalogue holds them with no further change. The page cannot be opened for a consignment it does not apply to. Its help gains a second place to find the number, the hint loses its punctuation, the boxes stop browsers offering saved values, and a trader can save the page blank and move on, with the gap held at submission instead. The page is a step of the consignment addresses section: opened from that page and always returning to it. The plants frontend has no CPH number and is not changed. Every changed English string gets its Welsh machine draft in the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: A live-animals consignment holding cattle or fish is asked for a CPH number, and its consignment addresses page has a CPH section; one holding only horses, cats or dogs is not asked and its consignment addresses page has no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001, p9-002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-110; trace:e2e p6-068, p6-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-025, p1-057; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-017, p2-026)
Opening the CPH number page for a consignment the question does not apply to sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106)

The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' a link to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-009; trace:animals-fit p13-018; trace:e2e p6-084)

The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and still describes the whole group of three boxes (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-010; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-119; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-040; trace:animals-fit p13-007)
Each of the three CPH boxes turns browser autocomplete off and carries the pattern [0-9]* alongside the numeric input mode (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-012; trace:animals-fit p13-014)

Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty shows no error: any saved CPH number is cleared, the trader returns to the consignment addresses page, the CPH section there stays incomplete, and the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-014, p9-015, p9-004, p8-135)

The CPH page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page however the page was reached (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-117; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-043; trace:e2e p6-078)

increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 reads a germinal product's total gross weight, package count, temperature and identification details back on the review.
