increments.title: A draft's review shows the view header with its Draft status and stays editable
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads a draft's review the way it heads a submitted notification's view, and keeps it editable with what is still incomplete listed. The 9 October ruling keeps that content, keys the header on the real service's one review route and the stored status, and keeps dashboard draft rows going to the hub (c-246). Today a draft's review, reached from the hub's 'Review and submit', has the journey heading and the status strip and no header. Afterwards the same review, for a Draft, shows the view header drawn in the set's own template with the status strip off: the Draft tag, the reference as heading, the date created, Copy as new, Delete and the Import reference numbers, and stays editable.
acceptanceCriteria: A draft's review, reached from the hub's 'Review and submit', shows the notification reference as the h1 with a 'Draft' tag beside it, in place of the 'Review your notification' heading and the status strip (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-008, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-009; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-089, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-104; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-096, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-097; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-063, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-064; c-246)

Under the header the draft's review shows 'Date created: <d Month yyyy>', the date the notification was created (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-012; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-104)

The draft's review header offers 'Copy as new' and a red 'Delete' warning button that opens the notification's delete confirmation, and no 'Amend this notification' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-009; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-104; c-246)

The draft's review shows the 'Import reference numbers' section with its warning and the 'Notification reference' and 'Customs document code' rows as selectable text, as a submitted notification's view does (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-104; c-246; c-294)
Every card on the draft's review has a Change link to its question page (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-105; repo:tests repo-tests-p3-110)

When the draft has incomplete sections, the review shows a 'There is a problem' error summary listing each one, each entry linking to its card, and an error message under each incomplete card's heading (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-105, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-106)
The draft's review ends with a Continue button (prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-106; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-001)

A live-animals draft's review has a Back link to the live-animals notification list, the set's own list in the animals frontend (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-081; c-143; c-246)
On the notification list, a draft's row still opens its overview hub, not the review (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-097; repo:tests repo-tests-p3-111; c-246)

A high-risk plants draft's check answers shows the same header as the submitted view, with a 'Draft' tag, the reference as heading, 'Date created: <d Month yyyy>', the delete button and the 'Import reference numbers' section, and no shared status strip; its Change links, its errors and Continue stay, and it offers no 'Copy as new' (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-042, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-063; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p8-003, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-038)
notes: Re-drafted for the 9 October afternoon ruling: the Back link goes to the set's own notification list in the animals frontend (c-143), so it is observable the same way in every environment, and the import reference rows carry no Copy buttons (c-294; req-1986 waits on design). The header is drawn in the set's own review template with the strip switched off; the shared layout is not changed. Kept apart from the submitted-view header row (inc-111) because it reuses that row's header and the header-actions row's Copy as new, Delete and Import reference numbers (inc-112), so it follows both. The incomplete-card messages are the review cards row's (inc-101) and Continue is the review-ending row's (inc-110); this row shows they hold under the draft's header.
req-2004 (plants' draft view header) is added here by the combiner, under ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 47.

increments.title: Waiting on design: a Search button beside the country of origin, port of entry, transit country and place of landing searches
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 presents the country of origin control as a search box with its own button. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes this a JavaScript-era mechanic beyond the component's own options, so it waits on design question 1, as one waiting-on-design increment shared with the port of entry and transit country boxes. If design asks for it, the box gains a separate 'Search' button on the origin page of both animals sets and of plants; if design drops it, this row is dropped. Design Release 2.1 gives its type-aheads a separate Search button. A separate button is beyond the accessible-autocomplete's own options, so the 9 October afternoon ruling puts it to design as question 1. When design answers, it is built as design says, in the animals port of entry and transit country searches and the plants place of landing search, or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, the live-animals and plants origin pages' country boxes each have a separate button at their right, showing a search icon with the visually hidden text 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-032; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-031; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-063, p3-021; conflicts:c-009)
Without JavaScript, both pages still show the plain labelled 'Country of origin' select and save the chosen country, with no Search button (conflicts:c-006; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-046)
With Welsh chosen, the button's hidden text shows its Welsh counterpart on both pages (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-117; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p5-042)

With JavaScript, the port of entry search and the transit country search each have a search button beside the box whose accessible name is 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-026, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-070; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-013, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-053)

In the plants frontend, with JavaScript, the place of landing search has the same search button with the accessible name 'Search' (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-035, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-023)
Without JavaScript, the three questions are still labelled native selects that choose and save an answer, with no search button (conflict c-006; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-103)
openQuestions: Design question 1 (search buttons): design must say whether the separate 'Search' button beside the country of origin, port of entry and transit country boxes is needed. Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it. No safe default: the ruling puts it to design.

Design answers design question 1 (search buttons) of the 9 October afternoon ruling: is a separate Search button beside the type-ahead strongly needed, and from which tested library? Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it.
notes: Combines the drafts of the start-and-origin, arrival-and-transit areas for this row: they change the same page, record or set-up, so building them apart would repeat it.

Depends on inc-009 (the hint and placeholder on the same control). The button is a change to the shared accessible-autocomplete component in each frontend.

increments.title: Country of origin results take the prototype's screen-reader wording, if design says the component's own cannot stand
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 labels the country results 'Country search results' and announces 'Selected <country>' on a choice. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the accessible autocomplete's own announcements now (req-1909) and puts this custom wording to design as question 13. If design says the component's own announcements cannot stand, the origin page of both animals sets and of plants takes the custom wording; otherwise this row is dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, on the live-animals and plants origin pages, the country results are labelled 'Country search results' for screen readers, and choosing one announces 'Selected <country>', for example 'Selected France' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-036, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-037; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-066, p3-021; conflicts:c-009)
With Welsh chosen, the results label and the selection announcement show their Welsh counterparts on both pages (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-117; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p5-042)
openQuestions: Design question 13: design must say whether the accessible autocomplete's own result and selection announcements can stand. The custom wording is built only if design says they cannot; otherwise this row is dropped.
notes: New row: req-020 leaves inc-009 because it is now blocked on design question 13 (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-066). Kept apart from the Search button row because it waits on a different design question. If the arrival-and-transit area drafts the same question for the port and transit boxes, the combiner may merge them into one waiting-on-design row.
Depends on inc-009. The wording is a change to the shared accessible-autocomplete component's messages in each frontend.

increments.title: Region code prefix follows the picked country in the browser, if design asks for it
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 writes the region code prefix the moment the user picks a country, and shows an empty prefix slot before any country is chosen. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the origin page now with the server-side prefix DR1 shipped and puts the live prefix and the empty slot to design as question 2. If design asks for them, with JavaScript the prefix follows the picked country with no submission; if design drops them, this row is dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, picking France in the country box makes the region code prefix 'FR', and then picking Netherlands makes it 'NL', with no form submission (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-047, p2-048; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-049, p2-050; conflicts:c-008)

With JavaScript, before any country is chosen, the revealed region code box shows an empty prefix in front of it, which fills in once a country is picked (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-052; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-048; conflicts:c-008)

Without JavaScript, the prefix still shows the saved or submitted country's code once the page is re-shown, as DR1 shipped it (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-008; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p5-026; conflicts:c-008)
openQuestions: Design question 2 (region code): design must say whether the region code prefix should follow the picked country live in the browser, with an empty prefix slot before a country is chosen. Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it.

increments.title: Once commodities come from MDM, the germinal catalogue holds V4's 18 items, with embryos and ova separate and each its own GBN-AG type
increments.detail: V4 sets which germinal commodities the data applies to, and the GBN-AG schema has separate EMBRYO and OVA codes, so embryos and ova become separate items. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes this catalogue wait until commodities come from MDM and the germinal catalogue is re-distilled from that list. When it lands, the germinal catalogue holds V4's 18 items, each offering the species Design Release 2.1 lists, selections show as the live-animal search shows them, and each germinal trade line on GBN-AG carries the code for its own product type.
acceptanceCriteria: The germinal catalogue holds 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); 'Cattle, Semen' (05111000); and 'Cat, Semen', 'Dog, Semen', 'Goat, Semen', 'Horse, Semen', 'Pig, Semen', 'Rabbit/Rodent, Semen' and 'Sheep, Semen' (05119985). There are no Cat or Dog embryos or ova and no poultry, fish or bee germinal products. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-050 to -p1-063; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-037, -p1-038; conflict c-230 default)

Each germinal item offers the species Design Release 2.1 lists for its animal: Cattle offers Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, with Bovidae as well for semen; Horse offers Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat Capra hircus; Pig Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep Ovis aries; Cat Felis catus; Dog Canis familiaris; and Rabbit/Rodent, Semen one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-138, -p2-141 to -p2-143, -p2-145 to -p2-155-m1, -p3-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-061, -p3-062)

Ticking Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a 'Bos taurus' chip, as the live-animal search does. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-063; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-012)

In the published GBN-AG payload each germinal trade line carries the typeCode SEMEN for a semen item, EMBRYO for an embryos item and OVA for an ova item, and embryos and ova are always separate trade lines, never one 'Embryos/Ova' line. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-036 to -p1-039; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-028)
openQuestions: Blocked on MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2): commodities must come from MDM and the germinal commodity catalogue and search be re-distilled from that list before this row can be written for real. Until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927) with interim typeCodes (req-1928).

c-230: does the germinal catalogue hold only V4's 12 germinal commodities, or also Design Release 2.1's Cat and Dog embryos and ova? Default, carried here: V4's 12 with embryos and ova split and 'Semen - Dog or Cat' shown as separate Cat, Semen and Dog, Semen, 18 items; Cat and Dog embryos and ova are not offered.
notes: Combines V4's catalogue (req-093), its selection panel (req-1783) and the separate EMBRYO and OVA trade lines (req-1800): all three wait on the same MDM catalogue and change once it lands. req-1800 leaves the Commodity details row (inc-017), which now carries the interim codes (req-1928).

A new row: it holds the blocked half of inc-016 (ruling claim pm-p2-012). Depends on the draft row 'The germinal commodity page offers today's 12 germinal lines, and the live-animals page no longer does' (inc-016) and 'Germinal Commodity details asks total gross weight, number of packages and temperature, and the backend stores them' (inc-017), and on whichever row brings MDM commodities to the live-animals catalogue (inc-012).

increments.title: Waiting on design: the germinal dates' 'Choose date' calendar
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 renders the germinal collection and production dates with the MoJ date picker's 'Choose date' calendar. MoJ advises against its date picker for dates a user reads from a document, so the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the dates now as single text inputs and asks design (question 12) whether the calendar stays, or a plain date field or the GOV.UK date input will do instead. This row builds what design answers, enhancing the text inputs built now, or is dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: If design keeps the calendar: each germinal date field has a 'Choose date' toggle opening a month grid with previous and next year and month buttons, 'Select' and 'Close', and picking a day fills that date's text input; without JavaScript the text input works as before. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-076; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-096, -p1-108)

If design answers that the GOV.UK date input will do instead: each germinal date is asked as Day, Month and Year fields, and the V4 date checks of the single-input row still apply to the date they make. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-096, -p1-108)
openQuestions: Waits on design's answer to design question 12 (germinal dates): whether the MoJ date picker's calendar stays, or a plain date field or the GOV.UK date input will do instead. Built as design says; if design answers a plain date field, nothing changes and the row is dropped (ruling 9 October afternoon, claims 57, 96 and 108).
notes: A new row, split from inc-053 by ruling claims pm-p1-055 and pm-p1-096. It belongs in the waiting-on-design theme ('Waiting on design: JavaScript-only behaviour from the prototype', claim pm-p1-056), not germinal-products, and depends on inc-053, whose no-JavaScript text inputs it builds on (claim pm-p1-057).
The MoJ frontend package is already a dependency of the frontend.

increments.title: Party pickers filter as the trader types
increments.detail: With JavaScript, narrows a party picker's list as the trader types, with no page reload, on the live-animals pickers and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, as DR1 and Design Release 2.1 both wanted. It waits on design: until design, with the product owner, answers design question 5, the server search behind the submit button is the whole search. It is built as design answers, or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, typing in the search box of an animals party picker hides, without a page reload, every row whose name, address lines and country do not contain the typed text in any case, and the results count updates to match (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-074, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-075, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-076; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-054)

The high-risk plants consignor and place of destination pickers filter in the same way as the trader types (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-028; repo:plantsfrontend repo-plantsfrontend-p6-037)
With JavaScript turned off, submitting the search still narrows the list on the server (document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-052, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-054)
Clearing the search box shows every row again, and the count returns to the full total (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p6-102)

If design keeps it under question 5, with JavaScript the address book list asks for its rows again as the user types in the search field or changes the Type select, and swaps in the table, the results line and the pagination without a full page load, on top of the search form that already works without JavaScript; if design drops it, nothing changes (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-026, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-055, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-071; c-169)
openQuestions: Design, with the product owner, must answer design question 5 (live filtering as the trader types) before this builds; if design drops it, this row is dropped. Until then the server search behind its submit button is the whole search (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm).
notes: New on this re-distil: split out of the role-filtered pickers row because req-592 now has blockedBy (ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm, c-094), so the rest of that row can build now. The place of origin's as-you-type country filter waits the same way but is req-1951, not this area's. req-592 also names the germinal products set's pickers: if this row builds before the germinal copy (req-1827) is taken, the copy inherits the filter; if after, the germinal pickers need the same change in the germinal-products theme's code, which this row does not touch. Client-side code is new; neither frontend's picker carries JavaScript today. Depends on the role-filtered pickers row (one page to filter) and the picker layout row (the results count it updates). Theme: consignment-parties.

One increment for design question 5, as ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 15 says: the party pickers' live row filter (req-592) in both animals sets and plants, and the address book list re-requesting as the trader types or changes Type (req-2039, added by the combiner).

increments.title: Waiting on design: address search's search-only layout, results as the trader types, reveal on a pick and its announcements
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's search pages show only the search at first: the address fields and the uses checkboxes appear once a result is picked or the trader chooses 'Enter address manually', the search hides after a pick, and screen readers hear how many results there are. The 9 October afternoon ruling (c-287) holds these back as one waiting-on-design increment: design question 10 asks whether address search keeps this search-only layout or uses the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible, and the custom announcement is beyond the component's own options. They also wait on the address lookup, like the rest of address search (c-217). Built on the server-submitted search (the row before), as an enhancement of a page that already works. Design Release 2.1 opens Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses on the address search alone, lists matches as the user types, and reveals the address fields once a result is picked or 'Enter address manually' is chosen. This is JavaScript-only behaviour, so Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling holds it as one waiting-on-design increment: design is asked (question 10) whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do. It is also blocked on the address lookup becoming a real feature. If design keeps it, it is built on top of the no-JavaScript search, which keeps working without JavaScript.
acceptanceCriteria: Below the address search, an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button reveals the address and contact fields without picking a result (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-045)

On the search pages the address fields and the 'What else should this address be used for?' checkboxes stay hidden until the trader picks a result or chooses to enter the address manually, the search box hides once a result is picked, and the fields show again after a failed submit when anything was entered or picked (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042-m1, p7-049; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-070)

Submitting a search page before picking or entering anything shows, in order, 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number', with no country error and no error of the search's own, and reveals the fields so each error summary link reaches a visible field (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-051; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-071; conflicts:c-109)
Screen readers hear the result count through a polite live region, such as '1 result available' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-047)

With JavaScript on, for 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141)

Typing in the address search lists matching addresses below it in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as the lookup's formatted address line with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '1 result available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-178)
Below the address search an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button reveals the address and contact fields (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-085, p16-130)

Saving the search-only layout with nothing picked or typed shows the six field errors with the address and contact fields revealed, so each error summary link moves to a visible field; the errors stay until the next save, and the typed values, ticked uses and search text are kept (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092, p16-094; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-180)
With JavaScript off, the page behaves as the no-JavaScript search does: the fields are shown and the search button searches on the server (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-090; c-305)

If design keeps it under question 10, with JavaScript address search results appear as the trader types, with the typed text in bold in each result (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-046; c-287)

If design keeps it under question 10, picking a search result hides the search, reveals the address and contact fields and announces 'Selected <name>' to screen readers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p16-033, prototype-dr2-1-source-p16-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-087; c-305)

increments.title: Waiting on design: the amend and cancel-amendment pop-ups
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 opens the amend and cancel-amendment confirmations as modal dialogs over the current page. GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, the Ministry of Justice's Modal dialog is not accepted (Experimental, no documented fallback without JavaScript), and no increment writes custom JavaScript to copy the prototype. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the confirmations now as pages carrying the pop-ups' wording, and holds the pop-ups themselves as one waiting-on-design increment for both animals sets and plants, blocked on design question 9. The expected answer is that they are not built, and the increment is then dropped; it is built only if design makes a strong case, as design then says.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, 'Amend this notification' and 'Cancel amend' open their confirmations as modal dialogs over the current page instead of going to the confirmation pages, each hidden until opened, announced as a modal dialog named by its heading (the amend dialog also described by its question), with a Close (X) button announced as 'Close' and an overlay (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-029, prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-030, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-050; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-183, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-060, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-061)

Close, the overlay and the dialog's 'No, go back' or 'Go back' dismiss it without acting and leave the trader where they were (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-054, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-084)
With JavaScript turned off, the same controls still reach the amend and cancel-amendment confirmation pages and work as before (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-088)
The same dialogs and fallbacks apply in the high-risk plants frontend (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-088)
openQuestions: Design question 9 (design must answer): are the amend and cancel-amendment pop-ups built at all, and if so with which tested component? Expected answer: not built, and this increment is dropped. Built only if design makes a strong case; MoJ's Modal dialog is not accepted (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 7 and 19).
notes: New row from the 9 October afternoon ruling, claim 19 (p1-088): the pop-ups leave inc-120 and inc-121 and wait here in the waiting-on-design theme. Depends on the amend confirmation row (inc-120), the cancel-amendment row (inc-121) and the Amend status bar row (inc-122), whose no-JavaScript pages it would enhance. req-1391's dialog half, req-1392's closing and req-1414's dialog half are built here only if design says so; their page halves are built in those rows. Changes plants too when built (claim 8). The germinal set's copy follows inc-185.

increments.title: Waiting on design: the place of origin picker's rows filter as the trader types
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 narrows the place of origin picker's rows as the trader types or picks a country, with no page reload.
